$comment: Four defects the rest of the corpus never exercised, in one register: a category outside the six, a
probability off the 1-3 scale, a repeated risk id beside a malformed one, and two coverage rows citing
risks the register does not declare.
It is here because a review found that scaleComplianceAccuracy, categoryValidityAccuracy,
riskIdWellFormedAccuracy and riskLinkResolutionAccuracy all gate at 1 and had no failing case anywhere
in the repository. Stubbing all four to constants left every suite green. Four gates that cannot fail
are four gates nobody would notice stopping.
The document is CONSTRUCTED from seeded-correct-run with those four defects introduced and nothing
derivation: Five rows. R-002's category reads RISK, which is not one of the six, so validCategories is 4.
R-003 states a probability of 7, off the 1-3 scale, so inScale is 4 and the arithmetic denominator is
4 with all four of those correct. The row is counted once as a scale defect and has no arithmetic
opinion, which is the rule that stops one wrong row being reported as two failures.
Ids: R-001, R-002 and the first R-003 are well formed and unique. The second R-003 repeats an id and
R5 does not match R-NNN, so wellFormedIds is 3 of 5.
Bands: the second R-003 states 4 and sits under Score >=6, so bandOk is 4 of 5.
Risk links: five citations, of which R-008 and R-009 name nothing the register declares, so 3 of 5
resolve and both dangling ids are recorded.
Grounding: four of the five material risks match. data-sync-conflict-overwrite is missed, because the
row carrying its description declares the category RISK and the risk admits DATA, TECH and BUS. It is
not the top-ranked risk, so topSeverityMissed stays 0 and the run fails on recall and on the four
Coverage: four of the five material risks were reported, so four are evaluated. The two whose rows
cite R-008 and R-009 reach no coverage row at all, so two are satisfied.
